"Has Legs With Which To Stand"
Sacramento Poetry Center - Poetry Now
Poetry
Feb 4, 2019

“Has Legs With Which To Stand”

The white Stork struts and strolls on long legs.
Pink Flamingo dancers have strange and unique habits.

Has a leg to stand on.
Once upon a time.
When mimicking mime.
Dumb ventriloquists sublime.
Love is for the divine.
I heard this in a clock tower’s hourly chime.

Years and days pass so slow.
Here below, the sky above.
I’m reading what is written.
The world’s splits, spinning ahead.

The sun is red and never was led.
Plastic covers the shores, it was said.

Something bathers ignore.
Asking what’s it all for?
Less than more.
Went to a bodega’s grocery store.
Music pouring from my roof.
Which I abhor.

Yet, peculiarly, I adore it.
Pacing my living room floor.
Watching all the golden gore.
No writing on the walls anymore.

Jon Billet

text.text:
I highly suggest those who are members of the Sacramento Poetry Center cancel your memberships immediately.

Through a blatant coup, a new board named themselves, shoving out the most long-term volunteers on the board (who together make up 90 years of experience in serving on the board), without allowing paying members to have a voice in the operation (who desperately wanted a voice). It was very shady and underhanded, and something I’ve never heard of happening in similar non-profits. They also drove out a number of women who served on the board previous to this final massive overtaking, ultimately leaving only one (new) board member that identifies as a woman.

It was a truly appalling power grab. DON’T give them your money.

New poetry groups shall form and I suggest you keep a look out for those.

text.text: The production was great, street parking wasn't too bad and there are a few spots (maybe 20?) in front of the theater, but the theater entrance is right by the light rail tracks, so be vigilant and watch your little ones! I marked it 3 stars because of the light rail, also because the theater was so hot! The cast and producers did hand out paper fans, which was a nice touch and for this particular production (Dusty Winds), it felt like you were sweating it out in the old west desert with them! I would go to a fall or a spring production there. Hmm, but maybe not another summer.

text.text: Just this past year, I have found out about Resurrection Theater and seen two different shows! I appreciate that this local theater company produces shows that are really thought provoking, powerful, and engaging. Every show I’ve seen has had talented casts and crew, creative sets, and very welcoming family vibe. A great date night out! Definitely check out their upcoming shows. Wherever they are producing it’s always a great time! Just bring a blanket/jacket or a cooling fan based on the time of year!
